title: Reliability: Test-Retest, Alternate Form, Inter-Rater, Internal Consistency, Cronbach's Alpha, KR-20
summary: Concept of reliability; types (test-retest, alternate/parallel form, inter-rater, internal consistency); Cronbach's alpha; Kuder-Richardson Formula 20; factors affecting reliability.
revision: Reliability = consistency. Types: test-retest, alternate form, inter-rater, internal consistency. SEM = SD × √(1 − r).
traps: SEM = SD × √(1 − r) — memorise the formula.

notes.t: The consistency or stability of test scores over time, across forms, across raters, or across items within a test.

r: Same test, two occasions, same group
Two or more raters score same responses

notes.t: A measure of internal consistency reliability based on the average inter-item correlation and number of items.
Cronbach's alpha ranges from 0 to 1. Higher alpha indicates greater internal consistency. Alpha ≥ 0.70 is generally acceptable for research; ≥ 0.90 for individual decisions.
KR-20 is a special case of Cronbach's alpha for dichotomous (right/wrong) items. It measures internal consistency for objective tests.

Worked example: Ten students take a test twice (one week apart). Scores:
Test 1: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 65, 72, 78, 82, 88
Test 2: 72, 74, 82, 84, 88, 66, 74, 80, 81, 87
Pearson correlation between Test 1 and Test 2 = r = 0.94.
Interpretation: r = 0.94 indicates high test-retest reliability — scores are stable over time.

SEM = SD × √(1 − r), where SD is the standard deviation of test scores and r is the reliability coefficient. SEM indicates how much an observed score may vary from the true score due to measurement error.

Worked example: SD = 10, reliability r = 0.81.
SEM = 10 × √(1 − 0.81) = 10 × √0.19 = 10 × 0.436 = 4.36.
Interpretation: The true score is likely within ±4.36 points of the observed score.
Reliability types, Cronbach's alpha, KR-20 and SEM are frequently tested. SEM = SD × √(1 − r) is a key formula.

OCR-extracted from source page 52 — Test-Retest Reliability Process:
1. Administer First Test: The same test is given to participants.
2. Wait for Time Gap: A period of 2 to 8 weeks is observed.
3. Administer Second Test: The same test is administered again.
4. Correlate Scores: Scores from both tests are compared.
5. Determine Stability Coefficient: The stability of test results is evaluated.
6. Evaluate Reliability: The test's reliability is assessed based on the coefficient.
